title: Stationary Points of a Cubic Function
subject: Mathematics

scenes.heading: Stationary Points of a Cubic
scenes.narration: Welcome. In this lesson we will find the stationary points of a cubic function, a question that appears in almost every Grade 12 Paper 1.

scenes.heading: What is a stationary point?
bullets: A point where the gradient of the graph is zero
It can be a local maximum or a local minimum
scenes.narration: A stationary point is a point where the gradient of the graph is zero. So at a stationary point, f dash of x equals zero. For a cubic, these are usually a local maximum and a local minimum, the turning points of the graph.

scenes.heading: Step 1: Find the derivative
scenes.narration: We are given f of x equals x cubed, minus three x squared, minus nine x, plus five. Using the power rule, the derivative is three x squared, minus six x, minus nine.

scenes.heading: Step 2: Set the derivative equal to zero
scenes.narration: Now set the derivative equal to zero. Divide every term by three to get x squared, minus two x, minus three, equals zero. This factorises to x minus three, times x plus one. So x equals three, or x equals negative one.

scenes.heading: Step 3: Find the y-values
scenes.narration: Substitute each x value back into the original function, not the derivative. f of negative one equals ten. f of three equals negative twenty two. So the turning points are negative one comma ten, and three comma negative twenty two.

scenes.heading: Step 4: See it on the graph
scenes.label: f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 5
scenes.narration: Here is the graph. At x equals negative one, the graph turns from increasing to decreasing, so negative one comma ten is a local maximum. At x equals three it turns from decreasing to increasing, so three comma negative twenty two is a local minimum. At both points the tangent is horizontal, because the gradient is zero.

scenes.heading: Exam tips
bullets: Always substitute into $f(x)$, not $f'(x)$, to get the $y$-value
Show the factorised form to earn the method marks
scenes.narration: Three exam tips. First, always substitute into f of x, not f dash of x, to get the y value. Second, write your coordinates with a semicolon, as the memo does. Third, show the factorised form, because that earns you method marks even if you make a small mistake later.
